name: Wilson's Disease
description: Wilson's disease is a rare inherited disorder that causes copper to accumulate in the liver, brain, and other vital organs. Most people with Wilson's disease are diagnosed between ages 5 and 35, but it can affect people of all ages.
prognosis: Excellent with early treatment; can be fatal if untreated
diagnosticMethods: Slit-lamp eye examination for Kayser-Fleischer rings
eli5Summary: Wilson's disease happens when the body can't get rid of copper properly, so copper builds up in the liver and brain. This can make people very sick, but taking medicine every day can remove the extra copper and help people live normal, healthy lives.
clinicalSummary: Wilson's disease is an autosomal recessive disorder of copper metabolism caused by ATP7B gene mutations affecting hepatic copper excretion. Clinical manifestations include hepatic disease (ranging from asymptomatic elevation of liver enzymes to fulminant hepatic failure), neurological symptoms (movement disorders, dysarthria, dysphagia), and psychiatric manifestations. Kayser-Fleischer rings are pathognomonic. Treatment with chelating agents (penicillamine, trientine) or zinc must be lifelong. Liver transplantation is curative for hepatic disease.
historicalBackground: Wilson's disease was first described by Samuel Alexander Kinnier Wilson in 1912. The genetic basis (ATP7B gene) was identified in 1993. The condition became one of the first genetic diseases to have effective medical treatment, with D-penicillamine introduced in 1956 by John Walshe.

recentBreakthroughs.title: Tiomolibdate choline phase 2 copper-balance trial published
recentBreakthroughs.description: Hepatology Communications (19 May 2026) published an open-label phase 2 in nine patients: daily copper balance fell significantly from day 4 with a cumulative mean decrease of −6.08 mg over 21 days, driven by increased faecal copper excretion; ALT elevations were mild and reversible.

recentBreakthroughs.title: ALXN1840 rolling NDA filed after neurologic data
recentBreakthroughs.description: Monopar began a rolling NDA to the FDA for ALXN1840 (tiomolibdate choline) on 22 July 2026. Phase 3 FoCus neurologic-subgroup data presented at AAN 2026 showed meaningful worsening at week 48 in 9% on ALXN1840 versus 25% on standard of care (p=0.038), with CGI-S improvement in 61% versus 17% (p=0.008).

recentBreakthroughs.title: UX701 gene therapy completes pivotal cohort 4
recentBreakthroughs.description: Ultragenyx completed enrolment of five patients in Cohort 4 of Stage 1 of the pivotal Cyprus2+ study of UX701 (rivunatpagene miziparvovec) in September 2025, spanning four dose cohorts; Stage 1 data are expected in Q4 2026.

recentBreakthroughs.title: AAV gene therapy trials initiated
recentBreakthroughs.description: First-in-human gene therapy trials using AAV vectors to deliver functional ATP7B copies show early promise.

recentBreakthroughs.title: New oral chelator development
recentBreakthroughs.description: Novel chelating agents with improved side effect profiles enter Phase II trials.
